name: Hohe Tauern National Park
blurb: Alpine meadows, ibex and marmots, and the vultures that clean up the high peaks.

tip.title: Thin out the marmots
tip.text: Marmots are a key prey for golden eagles and foxes. Set Alpine marmot to -100% and watch the eagle, the fox and the hares they then lean on.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Short alpine summers with strong light drive plant growth above the tree line.

nodes.name: Fungi, soil animals & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants, dung and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Rusty-leaved alpenrose
nodes.desc: A dwarf evergreen shrub that, according to Wikipedia, dominates the zone above the tree line in the park.
A low berry shrub of mountain heath and woodland edges. Red deer and hares are recorded eating it.

nodes.name: Mat-grass
nodes.desc: A tough tussock grass of acidic alpine pastures and meadows.
Colonial burrowing rodent that eats grasses, herbs and some insects, and hibernates for up to nine months. Wikipedia notes it was reintroduced to the park area.
Grazer of steep rocky slopes and high meadows, eating mostly grass and adding dwarf shrubs in autumn and winter. Golden eagles may take young.
Mountain goat-antelope and one of the main large mammals of the park, grazing alpine meadows and shrubs.

nodes.name: Red deer
nodes.desc: One of the main large herbivores of the park, eating shrubs such as bilberry as well as grasses.
Small herbivore of high ground, recorded eating bilberry; prey of foxes, stoats and golden eagles.
Generalist predator that hunts marmots, hares, voles and insects at all elevations.
Small weasel that hunts voles and other small mammals.
Omnivorous crow that eats insects and also feeds on carcasses.
Soaring scavenger that Wikipedia lists among the park raptors; feeds on carcasses of large mammals.
Specialist scavenger living mostly on bone and marrow from carcasses. Reintroduced to the Alps from 1987 and now breeding again.
Top aerial predator of the Alps, nesting near the tree line and hunting alpine pastures for marmots and hares.

story: Hohe Tauern National Park stretches for 100 kilometres along the Hohe Tauern mountain range in Austria and covers an area of about 1,834 square kilometres. It is the largest nature reserve in the Alps and features glaciers, waterfalls, extended tundra areas, and forests.
matters: The park shelters diverse alpine flora and fauna, including chamois, Alpine ibex, red deer, griffon vultures, golden eagles, and successfully reintroduced populations of the bearded vulture and Alpine marmot.
